ABOUT PLAYSCOUT

Sources and ranking methodology

How each live data feed is collected, scoped, attributed and refreshed without mixing platforms.

Three live sources, three distinct scopes

Apple Marketing Tools RSS supplies US iOS/iPadOS App Store Games ranks and release dates. It contains no Google Play ranks. GamerPower supplies active giveaways, game keys, loot and beta access across its labelled platforms, including selected Android and iOS offers. FreeToGame supplies a free-to-play PC and browser directory. PlayScout never combines these into a synthetic ranking.

Daily Game Pulse

Game Pulse is a derived briefing layer, not a fourth ranking provider. Each edition selects three recent Apple releases and three leaders from Apple’s US iOS grossing chart. Apple lookup metadata adds ratings, age labels and larger artwork. The introduction, play pattern and starting tips are automatically synthesized and explicitly labelled; version-sensitive claims still require editorial verification.

Source links and update time

Each live channel shows the provider, platform scope, last successful fetch and a link to the API or source page. GitHub Actions refreshes snapshots every six hours, so Game Pulse receives at least one new edition each day. A failed request keeps the last good snapshot instead of publishing an empty list.

Ranking fields

Store rank, chart movement, editorial heat and recommendation status remain separate. Every changing value needs a region, platform, observed time and source record. A future Android ranking requires a permitted Google Play data provider and will appear as its own chart.

Images and video

Store artwork comes from Apple’s permitted metadata endpoints. YouTube paths point to the original host and creator. A specific video is used only when matched to the game; otherwise the card says “Find videos” and opens YouTube search. Public engagement counts are shown only when obtained through the YouTube Data API.

Collection workflow

  1. Fetch only permitted fields at a respectful rate.
  2. Store source URL, external ID, platform and observation time.
  3. Normalize identity without erasing the original source record.
  4. Keep rankings, offers and directories in separate data contracts.
  5. Publish only pages that meet the index-quality threshold.
TRANSPARENCY

Check platform and source

Apple rows are iOS/iPadOS only. GamerPower offers and FreeToGame catalog entries keep their own platform labels. Editorial claims and codes require separate verification.
